caseno: Appeal from Appellate Decree No. 227 of 1962.
lawyer:
Aminul Huq ----- For the Appellant.
Rabia Bhuiyan ----- For the Respondents.
parties:
Rakhal Chandra Sarkar ----- Appellant.
Vs.
Benode Haldar and ors ----- Respondents.
full_judgment:
2. The plaintiff's case briefly stated is that one Dijabar Kapalic was owner of the suit land and after his death his widow Solok Moni, who got the lands, settled it by pafta dated 30.9.1943 (Exbt. 1) with plaintiff No. 1, Rakhal Chandra Sarkar, father of plaintiff Nos. 2-6, and plaintiff No. 7, Biswanath Moral and after taking settlement the plaintiffs have been in possession of the suit land by themselves and through bargaders. That the defendants on 27.11.1957 have cut away illegally the paddies grown by the plaintiff on the suit land measuring 2.52 acres in plot Nos. 231, 248 and 127 causing a loss of Rs. 900/-. Hence the plaintiff brought the present suit for recovery of Rs. 900/- as damages from the defendants. Out of 9 defendants, defendant No. 1, Benode Halder and defendant No. 5, Tayeb Ali Molla contested the suit by filing separate written statements. The case of the defendant No. 1 is that the plaintiffs were never in possession of the suit land. That defendant No. 2 has been in possession of the suit plots Nos. 231 and 248 through his bargaders, Tayeb Ali, defendant No. 5 and Sohrab who have grown the paddy thereon and that plot No. 127 was cultivated by the bargader of Solok Moni, namely, the defendant No. 8, Nasaruddin Molla and that the kabuliyat (Exbt. 1) relied upon by the plaintiff is collusive and fraudulent document and was never acted upon. The case of defendant No. 5, Tayeb Ali is that the crop in plot No 127 was grown by Nasaruddin Molla, the bargader of Solok Moni and that the crop in other plots Nos. 231 and 248 was grown by the defendant No. 5 as bargader of Sukhomoy Halder, and that the plaintiffs have no title or possession in the suit land. 

 4. The learned Munsif thereafter found that the defendants contention that the landlord had been in possession of the land after auction purchase cannot be believed in the face of Exbt. 2(a). He, therefore, held that the landlords were never in possession of the suit land. The learned Munsif has found that Exbt. 'A', the registered kabala dated 5.11.1947 executed by Solokmoni in favour of Mhomoy, Exbt. B series the barga kabuliyats of different dates taken by the defendant, and Exbt. C, certified copy of kabuliyat, dated 5.11.1947, alleged to have been executed by Solokmoni were all bogus documents. He further found that Exbt. 1 is a genuine document under which the plaintiffs acquired title in the suit land, as according to him, Solokmoni got land in her possession after Ext. 2(a) and as the auction purchaser did not go into possession and Solokmoni cleared the clouds of her title by setting aside the sale. 

 7. On appeal by the defendants the learned District Judge, Khulna, who heard the appeal reversed the judgment of the learned Munsif holding that plaintiffs have failed to prove that they grew paddy in the suit land in the year 1364 B. S. The lower Appellate Court in arriving at the finding took note of all the exhibits submitted by the parties in the suit though he did not discuss it thoroughly about their implication. The learned Judge directed his attention to the evidence of the witness adduced by the parties with regard to the possession of the land and the growing of paddy. In this connection he found that no borga kabuliyat for the year 1364 B. S. was produced by the plaintiffs and after examining the evidence of P.W. 2, 3 and 4 he was of the view that there was a doubt regarding the truth of the plaintiff's case and that the evidence of P. Ws. is shake and unreliable. He held that the evidence adduced on behalf of the plaintiffs that the plaintiff party has been in possession of the suit land and that they grew the paddy thereon in 1364 B. S. is not worthy of reliance In this connection the learned Judge also took into consideration the evidence of D. W. 3 that Biswanath (plaintiff No. 7) and Rakhal (Plaintiff No. 1) did the works for setting aside the sale and also for delivery of possession through Court under section 37A of the B. A. D. Act but from this circular it cannot be said that the plaintiffs were in possession in 1364 B. S. of the suit land. On a discussion of the evidence of D. Ws. he found almost all of them to be unreliable holding that it is not improbable that defendant No. 5 and D. W. 5 Nowsher Ali, cultivated the suit land in 1364 B. S. and finally came to the conclusion that in the facts, circumstances and evidence in the Case the plaintiffs have failed to prove that they grew paddy in the suit land in the year 1364 B.S. and dismissed the suit.
